Content: ... Thus American development has exhibited not merely advance along a `text(single)` line, but a return to primitive conditions on a continually advancing frontier line, and a new development for that area. American social development has been continually beginning over again on the frontier. This perennial rebirth, this fluidity of American life, this expansion westward with its new opportunities, its continuous touch with the simplicity of primitive society, furnish the forces dominating American character...
Copyright: Source: Frederick Jackson Turner, “The Significance of the Frontier in American History,” `1893`
